What are Brent and WTI?

Brent is the global benchmark for roughly two-thirds of internationally traded crude, priced off North Sea grades and delivered through the Atlantic basin. WTI (West Texas Intermediate) is the US benchmark, priced at Cushing, Oklahoma, and generally reflects North American supply and demand. Because Hormuz moves mostly Middle Eastern crude that prices against Brent-linked grades, analysts watch the Brent–WTI spread — and tanker insurance and freight costs — as early signals of Strait disruption. The series above simulates such a move; it is not real price history.
